subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should durable wake `delivered` mean persisted ownership transfer to a canonical session-key `systemEvent`, even across session resets, or must delivery remain pending or generation-bound until the intended session consumes it?
rationale: Both interpretations are technically implementable, but they produce different persisted terminal-state, reset, recovery, and operator-observability contracts; source inspection and tests cannot choose that product policy safely.

options.title: Generation-bound consumption
options.body: Keep the wake pending or separately handed-off until delivery is acknowledged by the intended session generation, preventing old-session obligations from appearing after reset.

options.title: Queue ownership transfer
options.body: Approve the current enqueue-time `delivered` meaning and explicitly document that canonical-session resets do not invalidate internal wake events.

options.title: Defer durable handoff
options.body: Pause this PR5 slice until the broader durable runtime and reset lifecycle contract has maintainer sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Generation-bound consumption
recommendation.body: Keep the wake pending or separately handed-off until delivery is acknowledged by the intended session generation, preventing old-session obligations from appearing after reset.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing session-delivery queue and restart recovery semantics that define the receiving side of this contract.
